repositories.notes: Not published anywhere yet -- nothing to resolve tags against until droidtop actually publishes a base+sway image. sway's headless backend (WLR_BACKENDS=headless) is well-documented (ArchWiki, Gentoo wiki) and is already droidtop's own reference compositor (vendor/sway).

Not published anywhere yet. labwc supports WLR_BACKENDS=headless + WLR_LIBINPUT_NO_DEVICES=1 (labwc's own actions docs, real wayvnc use). A 2022 headless assertion-failure report (labwc/labwc#605) may or may not still apply to current releases -- not independently re-verified by droidtop.

Published by droidtop itself (images/primary/Dockerfile, .github/workflows/publish-primary-image.yml) -- debian:bookworm-slim + sway + seatd + a minimal dumb-init-based /sbin/init (droidspaces requires a real /sbin/init in the rootfs, confirmed from its own Documentation/Linux-CLI.md). officialSource=false since this is droidtop's own build, not Debian's own namespace. UNVERIFIED end to end -- never booted against a live droidspaces container (no rooted test device in this environment); see droidtop-boot.sh's own comments for the specific assumptions (env_file injection timing, seatd sufficing without systemd-logind).

Not published anywhere yet, and not recommended if it were: multiple open upstream issues report headless/virtual outputs broken on current Hyprland (hyprwm/Hyprland#7917, #8806) since it forked off wlroots onto its own Aquamarine backend in 2024. Listed for visibility/filtering, not as a working recommendation.

Official Arch Linux Docker image is amd64-only -- no arm64 build (confirmed via gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/archlinux-docker#29). Unusable on droidtop's ARM64 target as-is; a third-party rebuild (e.g. menci/docker-archlinuxarm) would need its own entry, not added here yet.
openSUSE's own Tumbleweed image lists linux/386, linux/amd64, linux/arm platforms; the ARM variant's exact architecture (armv7 vs. arm64) wasn't independently confirmed in this research pass.
Void's own current containers are at ghcr.io/void-linux/void-*, confirmed to publish linux/arm64 -- not Docker Hub's voidlinux/voidlinux, which is stale (unmaintained for years).
